title: Beach Air
address: 320 Reindeer Moss Ct, Myrtle Beach, SC 29588, United States
pain_quote_1:
I used to recommend Beach Air when they were locally owned. They were always fair, reasonably priced, and easy to work with. Unfortunately, my most recent experience after they were bought out (along with Waccamaw Heating & Air) was completely different.
I called because my unit was going into low pressure lockout. The technician looked at it for maybe 10 minutes and told me it had a leak. He said a pressure test would cost $700, evacuation and recharge of 7 lbs of refrigerant would be $1,400, and depending on what was leaking the repair could range anywhere from $100 to $4,000 — if it was even repairable. He also strongly suggested that since the unit is 10 years old, I should just replace the entire system.
When I declined replacement, he told me I’d have to schedule the pressure test and they were booked weeks out. With the cold weather we were having, I couldn’t wait.
I decided to investigate myself. I filled my nitrogen tank for $42 and as soon as I removed the service port caps, I could hear refrigerant leaking from the valve cores — something the technician should have easily noticed. I replaced both valve cores for $0.28 total. I pressure tested at 300 PSI overnight and the system held perfectly, confirming that was the only leak. I then vacuumed and recharged the system, and it has been working great ever since.
For comparison, I purchased 25 lbs of refrigerant for $200. Being quoted $1,400 for 7 lbs is excessive. Even more frustrating, when this company was locally owned, I paid around $300 for an evacuation and recharge.
On top of that, the technician argued with me that they “don’t work with home warranty companies and never have,” which is simply not true — they handled my warranty claims in the past and received payment directly from the warranty company.
Either this technician didn’t know what he was doing, or he was trying to upsell a major repair or full system replacement that wasn’t necessary. What turned out to be a simple valve core replacement could have cost me thousands — potentially $10,000+ for a new unit — had I followed their recommendation.
I won’t be calling them again and will be looking for another locally owned HVAC company. Very disappointed in how far they’ve fallen.

I want to share my most recent experience with Diamond Air, because it went from great to completely unacceptable.

No one ever showed up. When I called customer service, I was told there was “nothing they could do” because the year had expired. So much for the plan I paid for.

Recently, I called again due to a loud noise coming from my system. A technician came out and diagnosed a blower fan wheel issue. I had the technician recheck it, and he confirmed it was incorrect and needed to be reordered, delaying the repair another day.

To make matters worse, I was never given a clear breakdown of charges. Everything was billed as a single lump sum. Given that technicians are paid commission, this lack of transparency is extremely concerning.

Between the missed PM service, incorrect parts, inflated pricing, delays, and refusal to provide itemized billing, I will never use Diamond Air again.

Never again. Stay away.
